answer: One reporter, one press card. The national press council verifies the applicant's identity and job at a registered outlet, then issues a walnut-brown press card and signs a fresh challenge tying it to the agent's key, checked against the press register each epoch. A second key claiming the same card is rejected; the council holds the record, not the claimant. The register is the inlet where newsrooms check credentials before giving access. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 cards at $150 each, about $150,000 in all, plus a glacier of pay slips and ID checks no farm can fake overnight.
